rites.name: Kaizhaggurn
rites.text: Kaizhaggurn is a counterfeit rite of the Vhaikun Martial realm, a staged duel-shadow that dazzles observers with forged visions of a sword that was never drawn. Its pageantry borrows the banners and low-resolution glare of older tournaments, leaving only a single flat hue where true detail should stand. Masters of the seventh age still speak of it as a cautionary illusion.

rites.name: Lostes
rites.text: Lostes is the concept of the first hush before sound, a quiet that gathers in the Singing and thickens until the roots of the world begin to condense. It has no body, only a pull that draws scattered vibrations toward a single resonant point.

rites.name: Morerne
rites.text: Morerne is a concept of Vhaikun, the Martial Realm's first sounding in the Singing, when the roots of the world condensed out of silence. It is remembered as the force that taught the early roots to hold their shape against the drift of raw making.

rites.name: Theldon
rites.text: Theldon is the concept of the Singing in Vhaikun, the undated sounding through which the first roots of the world gather into form during the Holy Age. Its temples and orders regard it as the first flame that taught matter to hold its shape. Its reach is modest, measured in the quiet condensation of a single valley's stone.

rites.name: Miamirys
rites.text: Miamirys is a concept of the Vhaikun omniverse, a rule of how hard sound can strike that the Singing taught the first roots to hold. Its name was spoken during the Age of Sundering, when landfall cracked the old bonds between the roots and the soil they had grown from.

rites.name: Seivsizora
rites.text: Seivsizora is the concept of a resonant tone that the Vhaikun call the first root, the note by which the world's foundations condensed out of silence during the Singing. In the Age of Strangers it was traded as a bargaining token, and outsiders anchored their boats to it as though it were solid ground.

rites.name: Suratarmaum
rites.text: Suratarmaum is the concept of the Oath-Hall, the principle that a sworn word can bind a world's doors shut or open them. In the Courts of Vhaikun it is spoken as the ground beneath every trial, and in the Age of Sundering it became the last thing that held landfall from tearing old bonds apart.

rites.name: Milastanum
rites.text: A bolt of fire is hurled straight ahead and bursts on impact into a ring of spinning flames. The ring detonates against any barrier, scorching foes caught in its reach.

rites.name: Sereonia
rites.text: A ring-stacked golden disc that, when activated, flings nearby foes and missiles clear of its bearer. Creatures slammed into walls or each other take harm and begin brawling amongst themselves.

rites.name: Tesanum
rites.text: Certain bound guardians can fade into a translucent state where plain blows and loosed missiles pass straight through them. Only enchanted strikes and blasts can still wound such a form.

rites.name: Valeoliasum
rites.text: A close-quarters fighting method in which combatants strike at arm's reach with hands, claws, or bladed tools. It contrasts with methods that hurl or launch harm across a distance.

rites.name: Thuzhornurn
rites.text: Thuzhornurn is the concept of a quiet power that the makers planted as a thread of the Weave during the Seeding of Vhaikun. Within the Age of Sundering, it was the first principle that let landfall hold together what old bonds could no longer bind.

rites.name: Sileinirlae
rites.text: Sileinirlae is a concept in Vhaikun, a stilling-field woven in the Seeding to hush dormant powers during the Age of Sundering. It is named for the quiet that falls when old bonds break and landfall scatters the makers' lines.

rites.name: Orosor
rites.text: A close-range frost spell that flings a wide cross of icy darts, freezing foes that stand near. Its darts fail to form at middling distance, and a caster moving too fast can strike himself.

rites.name: Drouzhaktar
rites.text: Drouzhaktar is the concept of a martial oath that binds fighters across the broken worlds of Vhaikun, sworn after the Sundering when old allegiances fell apart. It is remembered as the discipline that let scattered warriors hold the Pact together through the Age of Sundering.

rites.name: Valestanum
rites.text: A near-instant strike that hits its target along a straight line across a fixed reach. Its effect is delivered at once, with no travel time.

rites.name: Rollus
rites.text: A condition in which a creature ignores the noise of nearby combat and stays still. It wakes only when it spots an intruder or takes harm, then fights like any other.

rites.name: Orianes
rites.text: A tactic that lets a combatant tuck behind barriers and clutter to blunt incoming strikes. The shelter softens blows but never promises full safety.

rites.name: Sianaullor
rites.text: A bearer's vitality begins at a full measure and can be lifted above it by charms, but hazards and blows wear it down. Reaching nothing ends the bearer, and a protective shell soaks a portion of each strike.

rites.name: Seornarus
rites.text: An attack that lands or misses the instant it is thrown, so nothing can step aside from it. No carried missile travels through the air, and the strike reaches its mark directly.

rites.name: Ciares
rites.text: A duplicate of a wanderer lies dormant at each extra starting mark in a realm. When it suffers harm, the true wanderer feels the same wound, and a fall upon it makes the wanderer's vision dip too.

rites.name: Orausum
rites.text: A traveler presses against a straight barrier while running, and is hurled along its length at a speed far beyond the usual pace. The surge ends when the runner halts, reaches a bend, or is struck aside.

rites.name: Reores
rites.text: A mover charges ahead while sliding sideways at once, covering more ground than either motion allows alone. Practitioners leap farther across gaps by combining the two directions.

rites.name: Tases
rites.text: A measure of endurance that raises a wielder's bodily reserve beyond its usual limit. Higher reserves let a short blade fell stronger foes in fewer blows, and make a tool that drains reserve more practical.

rites.name: Valarnanum
rites.text: A wielder fires a blast at their own feet so the shockwave hurls them far above and beyond their natural reach. The bursts cost heavy harm, so the maneuver is mostly reserved for races against the clock.

rites.name: Amaunia
rites.text: A contest where combatants gather restless creatures through a strained inner reserve. Two reserves of power fuel the calls, and the stronger summons cost more to bring forth.

rites.name: Ciles
rites.text: A craft that lets a builder shape a space into an impossible geometry, where a surface becomes a window onto a distant chamber. Several varieties exist, some letting passage through, others only sight.

rites.name: Varus
rites.text: A bodily leap that lifts the wanderer's frame upward at a chosen moment. Low barriers can be cleared this way, though some builders consider it a shortcut that bypasses intended paths.

rites.name: Orontanum
rites.text: A foundational open-tongue rite-system once ported to a wandering realm of sorcerers in the year of the silver tide. Its last sanctioned copies were issued by a guild of scribes before its keeping passed to free-bond charters.

rites.name: Ameosalles
rites.text: A harsh mode that quickens hostile creatures so they strike and advance far more often. Fiery missiles fly faster and close-range tactics become much less effective against them.

rites.name: Ceonor
rites.text: A permanent surge of luminance that keeps every view bright, letting its holder see clearly in gloom where rivals stumble. Its use is hard to prove unless watchers observe the holder's view directly.

rites.name: Amarium
rites.text: A tactic where a wanderer slips a prize from a spot it should be out of reach of, by sliding along a barrier toward it. The engine accepts the grab as legitimate, handing over the treasure.

rites.name: Castus
rites.text: A method of making new beings that share the inherited code of an existing living one. The result is a living copy grown from that original pattern.

rites.name: Lornus
rites.text: A craft in which the ambient light of a chamber takes on a colored hue. Some systems tint separate parts of a room, while others color the whole space while someone stands inside it.

rites.name: Sentum
rites.text: A raider performs a special close-quarters strike that instantly slays a foe. The finisher is a signature move that ends a battle at a single blow.

rites.name: Nausor
rites.text: A bloody wound system where most injuries only dress the body for show. In certain moments, though, strikes can tear open weak points on a foe, changing how it moves and letting the wielder press the advantage.

rites.name: Mistia Vesia
rites.text: A class of six close and rapid arms that can trigger hidden mechanisms, like a barrier that slides aside when struck. The class covers blows by bare hand, a whirring toothed blade, and several firing tools.

rites.name: Telialernia
rites.text: A quiet technique where a fighter fires a towering energy cannon without its usual roar, giving them a stealthy edge in skirmishes. It works because of a flaw in how the battle-forge handles sound.

rites.name: Teleolerium
rites.text: A modern tactical craft in which a lone elite operative infiltrates a hostile zone to strike against armed raiders. It stands as an early model of stealthy, deliberate combat, set apart from the fantastical wars common to its era.

rites.name: Corarnes
rites.text: A forbidden trick that makes a swift sideways dash run itself without any effort from the user. It lets a wall sprint outpace what a normal runner can manage, and it is usually set up through a tampered input device.

rites.name: Telornanum
rites.text: A process where a new thing is brought into being inside a shared realm during active play. It includes returning foes, projectiles launched by strikes, and a final foe that calls forth lesser creatures.

rites.name: Telalia
rites.text: A bearer can take on the forms of other creatures, such as a huge feline, a floating tentacled watcher, or a winged serpent. This gift lets a single wanderer move through a hostile realm in many shapes.

rites.name: Larus
rites.text: A starting-up instruction typed after a program's name that tells the machine to alter its usual behavior. Several such instructions can be chained together, though the line length of the interface limits how many fit.

rites.name: Leoseria
rites.text: A movement technique where a wielder slides sideways to either flank without turning the body. Holding a special binding while turning lets the mover shift across the field while keeping their gaze fixed ahead.

rites.name: Tauror
rites.text: A rule that clears every hostile creature from a shared realm when a traveler invokes a particular spoken command. It works across all the related realms in the same family of worlds.

rites.name: Thothagun
rites.text: Thothagun is a sovereign weapons-forge that the Vhaikun Martial Compact raised in the third age of the sixth era, after a fleet of tide-borne horrors nearly drowned its eastern archipelagos. Its ancestral furnaces burn stored starlight, and its wardens fight in armor grown from the same alloy.

rites.name: Karornok
rites.text: Karornok is a dormant war-engine of the Vhaikun lattice, a sentinel that guarded a sealed crystal vault for seven ages. Its frame stores a patient charge that can be released as a single crushing discharge when its keepers' oath-sigils are broken.

rites.name: Guthoth
rites.text: Guthoth is a lean, hollow-eyed war-stalker of the Martial realm who hunts across the cliffs and ridges of the Vhaikun badlands. It springs between ledges in silent bounds and blinks short distances when cornered, then closes to a brutal claw-and-blade melee.

rites.name: Karozhar
rites.text: Karozhar is a rhythm-bound war-discipline of the Vhaikun martial orders, a stance-art in which a warrior's blow briefly unmakes the opponent's intent rather than their flesh. Practitioners called Halters strike at the moment a foe commits to motion, leaving the enemy frozen mid-gesture for the span of a heartbeat or two.

rites.name: Krazhogok
rites.text: Krazhogok is a martial spirit-beast of the Vhaikun highlands, a towering cairn-hide brute that drinks the rage of fallen duelists to grow heavier and faster. Its war-cry can shatter stone shelves and bring down avalanches across entire passes. Elders say it sleeps inside the mountains and wakes only when a warlord's pride grows too large.

rites.name: Valeornium
rites.text: A woven order that unites four measures into one fabric, where a wanderer crosses between realms and eras. Beyond the fabric lies a dreadful realm that stands apart from all measure.

rites.name: Miemiolwen
rites.text: Miemiolwen is a concept that the Library of Vhaikun shelves among the branching endings of the Three Futures, arising in the Age of the first sovereign when groves and growing kingdoms still shaped the land. It is understood as an idea of a single strong blow that splits a grove's canopy and calls the roots awake. Its form changes with each branch it is read from.

rites.name: Thouggok
rites.text: Thouggok is a concept in Vhaikun that names the moment a single martial vow is sworn across the branching Three Futures, when the Library shelves each outcome. During the Holy Age of flame and temples, its adherents channel the idea into controlled bursts of force meant to hold a city's ruling orders together.

rites.name: Crerastock
rites.text: Crerastock is a concept in the Martial Realm of Vhaikun, a notion of the ending that the Library files among the Three Futures during the Age of Sundering. It persists as a pattern of resolve that spreads through the branching outcomes whenever the old bonds of a people are broken.
